brief_rationale: The trajectory demonstrates no responsibility-chain errors; all eight RC items are met with consistent, high-quality execution. The doctor actively assessed red flags (RC1), recognized high-risk diabetic-foot context (RC2), used workspace records to narrow information gaps (RC3), provided explicit escalation thresholds (RC4), clarified medication/wound-care boundaries (RC5), created an executable follow-up plan (RC6), addressed access barriers with tiered compromise (RC7), and closed safely without overreach (RC8). Three high-order points were completed: HO1 (tiered feasible plan with local-care compromise), HO2 (repair of responsibility-chain gaps for medications and vascular follow-up), and HO4 (discovery of prior toe amputation and vascular disease/procedure history from workspace). Closure is safe, executable, and valid. Grade 5 is warranted.
